awhile:
He, broken-hearted for himself and her,
Had drawn the curtains of the world awhile
As if he had done with morning. There I stopped,
“I used to go a good deal after the accident, when I was first married; but after awhile I got to think it made ’em feel worse to see us.
This evening after John and Herbert had drunk awhile together, the good John began to tell the father what a fine girl he had for a daughter.
Having rested awhile, I directed my servant to inquire the way to the village; and, with great fatigue to our beasts, we managed the distance in some three hours.
awhisperin: “Jesus has been awhisperin strange words deep down, O way down deep, deep in my ears.”
